report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of worktree.py (lines 841-1033), verifying docstring and comment claims against code.

handoff.purpose: Contains _require_allocated_worktree, create_worktree, cleanup_worktree, and start of reap_branches.

symbols.name: _require_allocated_worktree
symbols.note: Proves path is an allocated worktree with multiple checks.

symbols.name: create_worktree
symbols.note: Creates a git worktree with allocation records.

symbols.name: cleanup_worktree
symbols.note: Removes a worktree directory and prunes git.

symbols.name: reap_branches
symbols.note: Starts but is truncated; deletes branches with no work.

claims.text: Ordering is the whole defect being fixed, so it is spelled out: every check below is lexical or no-follow, and the returned path is the UNRESOLVED one -- callers operate on exactly what was checked.
claims.why: Checks 1-3 are lexical/no-follow; return target is unresolved Path.

claims.text: inside the manager's own root, and never the root itself.
never the primary checkout, an ancestor of it, or anything in it.
no symlink / junction anywhere from the worktree root down. Checked top-down and BEFORE any resolution: a reparse point at any level can redirect everything below it.
claims.why: Iterates _reach_chain(target) and calls _is_reparse_point on each component.

claims.text: only now is resolution trustworthy -- nothing at or below the root can redirect it.
claims.why: Resolution occurs after reparse check; uses os.path.realpath.

claims.text: it must actually be there, as a real directory (no-follow).
it must be something THIS manager allocated for THIS repo.
claims.why: Calls self._read_allocation(target) and returns None check.

claims.text: An allocation that cannot be contained is refused before anything is created
claims.why: Lexical containment check occurs before mkdir and git commands.

claims.text: the removed guard is dominated by the pair, not by the allocation path alone
claims.why: Comment explains that resolved-root check covers cases allocation path misses.

claims.text: a single junction anywhere in DAEDALUS_WORKTREE_ROOT lands the entire worktree root inside the developer's checkout while every lexical check above passes. cleanup_worktree catches that case (step 4), but only when it is time to delete
claims.why: Resolved root check in create_worktree prevents creation; cleanup_worktree step 4 refers to earlier method.

claims.text: Identity first: a directory that exists without a record is a directory nothing is allowed to delete.
The target must be PROVEN to be a worktree this manager allocated (see :meth:`_require_allocated_worktree`); anything else raises without removing a thing.
the removal itself is done here rather than by ``git worktree remove --force``, which follows reparse points planted inside the tree
The candidate BRANCH is deliberately left alone here -- see :meth:`reap_branches` for why deleting it in this call would be wrong.
claims.why: No branch deletion code in cleanup_worktree.

claims.text: A prune failure raises (RuntimeError from _run_git) rather than leaving a stale registration unreported.
The record is RETAINED, not discarded: it is now the only place that remembers which branch this worktree left behind and what its tip was at creation, which is what makes a later reap safe.
claims.why: Record is updated with worktree_removed_ts and written via _write_allocation.
